correctness.rationale: The KL chain rule with common random labels counts one marginal log 2 per first-round reveal and conditional entropy per second-round reveal, minus the joint entropy. Nearest revealed flanks screen distant observations, with the double correction at distance d counted at each of d−1 interior positions. Exponential decay at fixed ρ justifies the thermodynamic gap series. Expanding I_d in positive geometric modes yields the displayed factored positive second derivative; termwise differentiation is uniform in p for fixed ρ<1 since the denominators are bounded below by 1−ρ². The endpoint derivative at 0 is negative and that at 1/2 positive. In the geometric-flank representation, the linear and linear-log-scale terms of the small-argument binary entropy cancel. For p=t√δ the rescaled geometric flanks have uniform exponential tails on compact t-intervals, justifying the log-moment remainder and expectation convergence. The leading homogeneous bracket at independent unit exponentials is (U+V)h(U/(U+V)); the gamma sum has mean 2 and the independent uniform ratio has mean binary entropy 1/2. Thus the limiting scaled objective is t log 2+1/(2t). Its interior point has smaller value than either fixed bracketing endpoint, which by convexity localizes the true minimizers and proves convergence of values and minimizers. Bounded convergence at fixed p gives p log 2 and the stated relative penalty. These are forward path KL statements in nats; the length-first limit is essential.
